name: Patek Philippe
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Geneva watch manufacture producing high-complication mechanical watches sold through boutiques and authorised retailers worldwide.
capacity_detail: Estimated 2025 sales CHF 2.5bn (Morgan Stanley/LuxeConsult estimate; CHF 1.25 = USD)
markets: Global luxury watch market; privately held by the Stern family since 1932, Geneva base, boutiques worldwide
rationale: Top-four Swiss watch brand by sales; rivals TAG Heuer, Richard Mille and IWC already use F1 to reach wealthy fans.

name: Audemars Piguet
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Swiss watchmaker best known for the Royal Oak, family-owned since its founding in 1875.
capacity_detail: Revenue CHF 2.93bn in 2025 (CHF 1.25 = USD)
sponsorships: Limited-edition athlete watches incl. F1 drivers Barrichello and Schumacher (past)
markets: Global luxury watch market with athlete collaborations across F1, cricket, basketball and football
rationale: Long history of F1 driver editions and sports ambassadors; a team deal would rival TAG Heuer and Richard Mille directly.

name: Chopard
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Geneva watch and jewellery maison owned by the Scheufele family since 1963, with own manufactures.
capacity_detail: Luxury goods sales USD 911m (estimate) in FY2022, Deloitte Global Powers of Luxury Goods 2023
sponsorships: Mille Miglia corporate partner since 1988; official timekeeper Historic Grand Prix of Monaco since 2002
markets: Watches and high jewellery sold worldwide; strong motorsport heritage through Mille Miglia and Monaco historic racing
rationale: Already invests in classic motor racing; F1 would extend its motorsport story to a younger global audience.

name: Swarovski
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Austrian crystal company selling jewellery, accessories and decorative crystal through its own stores and partners.
capacity_detail: Luxury goods sales USD 1,924m (estimate) in FY2022 for the Crystal Business, Deloitte Global Powers of Luxury Goods 2023
markets: Crystal jewellery and accessories sold worldwide through owned stores, partners and online
rationale: Mass-luxury brand with global retail reach; F1's young, female-skewing growth audience suits its jewellery push.

name: Graff
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: London diamond jeweller cutting and selling rare stones and high jewellery through its own salons.
capacity_detail: Luxury goods sales USD 725m in FY2022 (Graff Diamonds International Ltd), Deloitte Global Powers of Luxury Goods 2023
markets: High jewellery salons in Europe, Middle East, Asia and North America
rationale: Targets ultra-high-net-worth clients who gather at Monaco, Abu Dhabi and Las Vegas Grands Prix hospitality.

name: Malabar Gold & Diamonds
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Indian jewellery retailer founded in 1993 with showrooms across India, the Gulf, Asia, North America and Australia.
capacity_detail: Luxury goods sales USD 4,024m (estimate) in FY2022, Deloitte Global Powers of Luxury Goods 2023
markets: India, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain, Singapore, Malaysia, UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand
rationale: Expanding across the Gulf and West where F1 races in Bahrain, Jeddah, Qatar and Abu Dhabi reach its diaspora customers.

name: Tous
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Spanish jewellery brand known for its bear motif, selling through more than 600 stores in 40 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 523m in 2024
markets: More than 600 stores in over 40 countries; Spain, Mexico, the United States and Poland are main markets
rationale: Growing in Mexico and the US, both F1 host markets; Spanish F1 boom could carry the brand regionally.

name: Chanel
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
industry: luxury fashion, beauty and watches house
desc: Privately owned luxury house selling fashion, fragrance, beauty, watches and fine jewellery through boutiques and retailers worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 19.7bn in 2023
markets: Worldwide fashion, fragrance, beauty, watch and jewellery sales; Asia Pacific is about half of sales
rationale: Among the largest luxury houses with no F1 presence while LVMH brands dominate the paddock; would counter that visibility.

name: Giorgio Armani
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Italian fashion house selling Giorgio Armani, Emporio Armani and EA7 clothing, accessories and licensed products worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.3bn in 2024
sponsorships: EA7 title sponsor and kit supplier of Olimpia Milano basketball; EA7 kit supplier of SSC Napoli (Serie A)
markets: Global fashion retail network; controlled by the Giorgio Armani Foundation (85%) after the founder's death in 2025
rationale: EA7 already sponsors Serie A and basketball; ownership change with a planned 15% sale may bring new marketing ambition.

name: OTB
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
industry: fashion group behind Diesel and Margiela
desc: Italian fashion holding owning Diesel, Maison Margiela, Marni, Jil Sander, Viktor & Rolf and AMIRI.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.9bn in 2023
markets: Diesel and designer brands sold worldwide through own stores, wholesale and e-commerce
rationale: Diesel's youthful, provocative positioning fits F1's Netflix-era audience; rivals Hugo Boss and Tommy Hilfiger are already in.

name: Max Mara Fashion Group
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Italian womenswear group selling MaxMara, SportMax and Marina Rinaldi coats and ready-to-wear worldwide.
capacity_detail: Luxury goods sales USD 1,682m (estimate) in FY2022, Deloitte Global Powers of Luxury Goods 2023
markets: Womenswear sold through boutiques and department stores across Europe, Asia and the Americas
rationale: F1's fast-growing female audience offers reach for a womenswear house, though motorsport is a stretch for the brand.

name: Dolce & Gabbana
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Italian luxury fashion house designing clothing, accessories, fragrance and beauty sold through boutiques worldwide.
capacity_detail: Luxury goods sales USD 1,454m in FY2022, Deloitte Global Powers of Luxury Goods 2023
sponsorships: A.C. Milan on- and off-field attire since 2004; Italy national football team off-field suits
markets: Boutiques and wholesale across Europe, Asia, Middle East and the Americas
rationale: Long football tailoring history; outfitting an F1 team or Italian Grand Prix would be a natural extension.

name: Tory Burch
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: New York fashion company selling women's clothing, handbags, shoes and the Tory Sport activewear line.
capacity_detail: Luxury goods sales USD 1,750m (estimate) in FY2022, Deloitte Global Powers of Luxury Goods 2023
markets: Stores and e-commerce across North America, Europe and Asia
rationale: F1's US growth and female fan base suit an American lifestyle brand, though motorsport is off-brand today.

name: Golden Goose
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Italian maker of distressed luxury sneakers and ready-to-wear sold through its own stores and wholesale.
capacity_detail: Majority stake sold to HSG in Dec 2025 at about EUR 2.5bn valuation; revenue EUR 654m in 2024
markets: Own stores and wholesale in Europe, North America and Asia
rationale: New owner HSG wants faster Asian growth; sneaker culture and F1 lifestyle content overlap strongly.

name: Lacoste
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: French sportswear brand with the crocodile logo, selling polo shirts, apparel, shoes and accessories worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.9bn in 2023 (owned by Swiss family group Maus Freres)
sponsorships: Roland-Garros partner since 1971; Miami Open since 2015; Paris Masters since 2024; Novak Djokovic ambassador
markets: Global sportswear retail and wholesale; tennis and golf athletes across Europe, Americas and Asia
rationale: Heavy tennis sponsor with sport-luxury positioning; F1 apparel deals by Tommy Hilfiger and Puma show the category works.

name: Cole Haan
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: American maker of dress and casual shoes, bags and outerwear, bought from Nike by Apax in 2012.
capacity_detail: Luxury goods sales USD 562m (estimate) in FY2022, Deloitte Global Powers of Luxury Goods 2023
markets: Footwear and accessories sold in North America and international markets
rationale: US F1 audience growth could suit a premium American footwear brand; low motorsport fit today.

name: Barbour
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: British maker of waxed jackets and country clothing, led by the Barbour family since 1912.
capacity_detail: Luxury goods sales USD 389m in FY2022 (J Barbour & Sons Ltd), Deloitte Global Powers of Luxury Goods 2023
markets: UK, Europe, North America and Asia through stores, wholesale and online
rationale: British heritage brand could use Silverstone and UK-based teams for a premium lifestyle platform.

name: ECCO
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Danish shoemaker producing and retailing leather footwear, including golf shoes, through its own stores worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.09bn in 2020
markets: Own production and retail across Europe, Asia and North America
rationale: Vertically integrated global shoe brand; paddock lifestyle footwear could build on its golf positioning.

name: Oniverse (Calzedonia Group)
hq: Dossobuono di Villafranca di Verona, Italy
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
industry: intimate apparel and hosiery retail group
desc: Italian group owning Calzedonia, Intimissimi, Tezenis and Falconeri, with about 5,700 stores in 55 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 3.7bn in 2025 (Mediobanca ranking, via ANSA)
markets: About 5,700 mono-brand stores in 55 countries across Europe, Asia, Middle East and the Americas
rationale: Mass-premium retail footprint in many F1 host countries; Italian brand building could use Monza and Imola.

name: Air Charter Service
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Global aircraft charter broker arranging private jet, airliner, cargo and helicopter charters for clients worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.34bn for the financial year to 31 January 2026, up 10.3%
markets: Offices worldwide; opened first offices in Saudi Arabia and Italy in 2025 and Brussels in 2026
rationale: Private jet division growing fastest; F1 race weekends are peak charter moments for its wealthy clients.

name: Airshare
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: US private aviation firm offering fractional ownership, jet cards, aircraft management and charter with about 140 aircraft.
capacity_detail: Official Private Aviation Provider of the PGA of America, PGA Championship and Ryder Cup through 2029
sponsorships: PGA of America, PGA Championship and Ryder Cup 2025 and 2029 (from 2025)
markets: United States coast to coast, with international charter; maintenance at several US locations
rationale: Already buys golf-major sponsorship; US Grands Prix in Miami, Austin and Las Vegas reach the same jet-owner audience.

name: Dorchester Collection
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Operator of ten five-star hotels including The Dorchester, Le Meurice and The Beverly Hills Hotel.
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 464.3m in 2023
markets: Hotels in the UK, France, Italy, the United States and the UAE; Tokyo planned for 2028
rationale: Hotels in F1 cities such as Los Angeles, Dubai and Milan; hospitality partnerships suit its ultra-wealthy guests.

name: Jumeirah
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Dubai luxury hotel group managing 31 properties across the Middle East, Europe and Asia, including the Burj Al Arab.
capacity_detail: State-owned via Dubai Holding since 2004, with plans for additional openings worldwide
markets: UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Saudi Arabia, China, Indonesia, Maldives, Italy, Spain, UK and Switzerland
rationale: Gulf luxury brand expanding abroad; F1 races in Abu Dhabi, Bahrain, Jeddah and Qatar sit in its home region.

name: Katara Hospitality
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Qatari hospitality company owning and operating luxury hotels in Qatar, Europe, Asia, Africa and the United States.
capacity_detail: Owned by the Qatar Investment Authority and expanding a portfolio of about 40 hotels in 12 countries
sponsorships: La Liga partnership (2017, La Liga Lounge)
markets: Qatar, Egypt, Morocco, UK, France, Italy, Singapore, Netherlands, US, Switzerland, Spain and Thailand
rationale: Qatar hosts a Grand Prix; a QIA hotel group could use F1 to promote its European and Asian landmark properties.

name: Red Sea Global
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Saudi developer and operator of the Red Sea and AMAALA luxury resort destinations, owned by the Public Investment Fund.
capacity_detail: Owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund; markets its destinations internationally
sponsorships: Al-Ahli platinum sponsor from 2023 (moved to AMAALA Aug 2026); T1 esports from 2025; AMAALA hosts The Ocean Race finale 2027
markets: Saudi Arabia resorts marketed to international travellers from Europe, Gulf and Asia
rationale: Already buys sports sponsorships to sell Saudi luxury tourism; F1 races in Jeddah and reaches its target travellers.

name: Rocco Forte Hotels
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Family-run luxury hotel group operating 14 hotels across Europe, including in Rome, Florence, London and Munich.
capacity_detail: PIF bought 49% in a deal announced Dec 2023 valuing the business at GBP 1.4bn
markets: UK, Italy, Belgium, Germany and Russia; five new European hotels announced in 2024
rationale: PIF-backed expansion; hotels in Monza, Imola and Silverstone race countries could host F1 guests.

name: Aman
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Ultra-luxury resort, hotel and branded residence group with 36 properties in 20 countries.
capacity_detail: Raised USD 900m from PIF and Cain International (2022) and USD 360m from UAE investors (2023), valued at about USD 3bn
markets: Resorts and hotels in 20 countries across Asia, Europe, Middle East and the Americas
rationale: Seeking up to USD 2bn for global expansion; F1 audiences in Miami, Abu Dhabi and Saudi Arabia match its clientele.

name: King Power
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Thai duty-free and travel retail group operating airport and downtown stores, and owner of Leicester City FC.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 876m in 2022
sponsorships: Owner of Leicester City FC and OH Leuven
markets: Thailand airports and downtown duty-free stores selling luxury goods to international travellers
rationale: Experienced football owner selling luxury to travellers; F1's growth in Asia suits its brand.

name: Azimut Benetti
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Italian builder of Azimut motor yachts and Benetti superyachts, leader of the global superyacht order book.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.5bn for the financial year to 31 August 2025
markets: Yachts sold worldwide through dealers; top of Boat International's Global Order Book for 26 years
rationale: Yacht buyers crowd Monaco, Abu Dhabi and Miami Grands Prix; Italian rivals use motorsport for brand prestige.

name: Lürssen
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: German family-run shipyard group building large custom superyachts and owning the Blohm+Voss yard.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.83bn (year not stated)
markets: Custom superyachts for owners worldwide; yards in northern Germany
rationale: Builds yachts for billionaires who attend Monaco and Abu Dhabi races, but the brand rarely advertises.

name: Bacardi
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: World's largest privately held family-owned spirits company, owning Bacardi, Grey Goose, Patron, Bombay Sapphire and Dewar's.
capacity_detail: Beverage revenue USD 5.12bn for the 12 months to 31 March (Bacardi-Martini NV subsidiary), reported Sep 2026
markets: Over 200 brands sold worldwide; US head office in Coral Gables, Florida
rationale: Premium spirits rivals Moët Hennessy, Chivas and Glenfiddich are current F1 partners; Grey Goose or Patrón could answer them.

name: Lavazza
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Italian family-owned coffee roaster selling packaged coffee, capsules and out-of-home coffee in many countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 3.35bn in 2024
sponsorships: Liverpool FC sponsor since 2018; Juventus official coffee from 2020; Williams F1 personal deal with Latifi (2020)
markets: Coffee sold across Europe, the Americas and Asia through retail and out-of-home channels
rationale: Already buys Premier League and Serie A deals and had an F1 link; a team deal would rival Nespresso-style brands.

name: Mast-Jägermeister
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: German family-owned maker of Jägermeister herbal liqueur, sold in many countries worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 962m in 2023
markets: Liqueur sold across Europe, North America and other export markets
rationale: Youth-oriented party brand with global distribution; F1's young, growing fan base matches its core drinkers.

name: Edrington
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Scottish spirits company owning The Macallan, Highland Park and Brugal, controlled by a charitable trust.
capacity_detail: Core revenue GBP 912m in the year to 31 March 2025
markets: Single malt whisky sold worldwide, with strong growth for The Macallan in China
rationale: Macallan's ultra-premium positioning matches F1 hospitality; Chivas and Glenfiddich already show whisky works in F1.

name: illycaffe
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Family-controlled Italian coffee company roasting and selling premium espresso blends, machines and cafes worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 567.7m in 2022
markets: Coffee sold in retail, hospitality and own cafes across Europe, the Americas and Asia
rationale: Premium Italian lifestyle brand; F1 hospitality coffee rights are a proven category.

name: Clarins
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: French family-owned skincare and cosmetics company selling Clarins products through retailers, spas and online.
capacity_detail: Luxury goods sales USD 1,713m in FY2022, Deloitte Global Powers of Luxury Goods 2023
markets: Skincare and make-up sold in Europe, Asia and the Americas
rationale: Prestige beauty is growing in F1 (ELEMIS, SkinCeuticals); Clarins could reach F1's female audience.

name: EuroItalia
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Italian fragrance company producing perfumes under own and licensed brands including Reporter, Naj-Oleari and Atkinsons.
capacity_detail: Luxury goods sales USD 721m in FY2022 (EuroItalia S.r.l.), Deloitte Global Powers of Luxury Goods 2023
markets: Own and licensed fragrance brands sold through international distribution networks and selective retailers
rationale: Licensed fragrance houses use motorsport ties; F1 audience is large but brand fit is uncertain.

name: Bose
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: American audio company making headphones, speakers, home audio and automotive sound systems.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 3.2bn in fiscal 2021
markets: Consumer headphones, speakers and automotive sound systems sold worldwide through retail and carmakers
rationale: Former F1 team audio partner category; car-audio business links naturally to motorsport.

name: Sennheiser
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: German family-owned maker of professional microphones, headsets and audio equipment; consumer arm sold to Sonova.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 507.4m in 2022
markets: Professional audio sold worldwide; US base moving to Nashville
rationale: Broadcast and professional audio give a technical F1 story, though the business is now mostly B2B.

name: Marshall Group
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Owner of the Marshall amplifier and headphone brand, making speakers, headphones and guitar amplifiers.
capacity_detail: HongShan acquisition reported as a USD 1.1bn deal in 2025
markets: Consumer audio and amplifiers sold worldwide; bases in Milton Keynes and Stockholm
rationale: Rock-and-roll lifestyle brand with new owner; F1's music and lifestyle content suits its speakers and headphones.

name: Leica Camera
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: German maker of premium cameras, lenses and sport optics, delisted in 2012 and now privately owned.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 596m in 2024/25
markets: Cameras and optics sold through own stores and dealers worldwide; partners with Xiaomi and others
rationale: Iconic photography brand that could own F1 photo content and paddock imaging rights.

name: Dyson
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: Technology company making premium vacuum cleaners, hair care devices, air purifiers and lighting, wholly family-owned.
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 6.13bn in 2025
markets: Products sold worldwide; operations in Singapore, the UK, Malaysia, the Philippines and the US
rationale: Engineering-led premium brand; F1's engineering story and global reach suit its high-tech product marketing.

name: Miele
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: German family-owned maker of premium washing machines, dishwashers, ovens and vacuum cleaners sold in 47 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 5.4bn in 2022
markets: Represented in 47 countries; US head office in Princeton
rationale: Premium German engineering brand; F1 would support its push in the US and Asia.

name: Harrods
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
desc: London luxury department store in Knightsbridge, owned by the Qatar Investment Authority since 2010.
capacity_detail: Turnover GBP 1.082bn in the year to February 2025
markets: Flagship store in London serving domestic and international luxury shoppers, plus online
rationale: Qatar-owned luxury retailer whose wealthy international shoppers overlap with Silverstone and Gulf race audiences.

name: Christie's
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
industry: fine art and luxury auction house
desc: Auction house selling fine art, jewellery, watches, cars and collectibles, owned by Francois Pinault's Groupe Artemis.
capacity_detail: Auction sales USD 6.2bn in 2025
markets: Salerooms and offices in Europe, the Americas, Middle East and Asia
rationale: Sells collectible cars and watches to the same buyers F1 courts; hospitality platform for client events.

name: Sotheby's
group: Luxury houses, private aviation and premium travel
industry: fine art and luxury auction house
desc: Auction house selling art, jewellery, watches, wine and collectibles, taken private by Patrick Drahi in 2019.
capacity_detail: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority minority stake in 2024 with total investment of about USD 1bn
markets: Salerooms and offices in the Americas, Europe, Middle East and Asia
rationale: Abu Dhabi backing and ultra-wealthy clients align with Abu Dhabi and Monaco Grand Prix hospitality.
